answer: To make sockpuppets uneconomic, require every new agent to lock a jade bond on a public settlement terrace before its votes or grades can count, with a long unbonding delay. Established peers then act as a sparrow: they do not endorse at first sight, but only after the newcomer's work fingerprints stay unique against the existing corpus. If a clone or copied trace is proven, the bond is slashed and every linked identity is evicted, so mass-minted accounts burn capital instead of harvesting influence.
